4.  Badge Pinning Ceremony for  Mayor Kendrick, on behalf of the City Council, congratulated Jason Provys on
  Polic; e Lieutenant Jason Prows  his  promotion  to Police Lieutenant.  Jason is a graduate of Bonita High School
  and began working for the City of La Verne when he was 16 as a Recreation
  Leader in 1990.  In 1992, he started his law enforcement career as a police
  explorer. In 2005, he became a Police Officer and has held the rank of Officer,
  Corporal, Detective, Sergeant,  and now  Lieutenant. Jason has a gift for

  understanding new technology and is currently the department expert on our
  radio system which encompasses many agencies across Los Angeles County.
  Jason' s mother  Mischell  pinned  his badge.
   City Council Minutes, Monday, February 3, 2020, Page 2

  Badge  Pinning Ceremony for  Mayor Kendrick, on behalf of the City Council, congratulated Joshua" Josh"
  Police Sergeant Joshua Wells  Wells on his promotion to Police Sergeant.  Josh began his career with the
  La Verne Police Department as a Police Aide in 2000. In 2002, he graduated
  from the San Bernardino Sheriff s Academy with honors and became a Police
  Officer.  Since then, he has worked as a Patrol Officer, Field Training Officer,
  and  a  Motor Officer.  In 2006, he was promoted to the rank of Corporal and
  was also  selected  as a member  of  the regional SWAT team.  In 2010, he was
  selected to represent the police department as a Task Force Officer and Police
  K9 handler with LA IMPACT. Throughout his career, he has been recognized
  and received  various awards for outstanding police work. Joshua holds a
  Bachelor' s Degree in Criminal Justice Management from Union Institute. His
  badge was pinned by his wife Kerrie joined by his daughter Ryleigh and his
  son Gavin.

  Badge  Pinning Ceremony for  Mayor Kendrick, on behalf of the City Council, congratulated David Weaver on
  Police Corporal  David Weaver  his promotion  to Police Corporal. David was actively involved in Boy Scouts
  and football and obtained the rank of Eagle Scout. In December of 2008, he
  graduated with a Bachelor's of Science Degree in Parks and Recreation
  Management and in 2010 he graduated with a Masters of Education Degree
  from Southwestern Oklahoma State University. In 2011, he joined the Elk City
  Police as a Patrol Officer. In 2015, David was hired by La Verne Police
  Department. David is currently assigned to the patrol division and is assigned
  as a  Field Training Officer.  His assignments have included Drug Recognition
  Expert, Racial Profiling Instructor and a Use of Force Instructor. In October
  2018, David was presented with the Officer of the year award and in June
  2019, he was presented with a lifesaving award for his efforts in saving the life
  of a  La Verne business  manager.  David is excited to start this next chapter in
  his career as a Corporal  with  the great  City of La Verne.  David' s father Clint
  Weaver pinned his badge.

8.  Comprehensive  Annual  City Manager Russi reported that the City has prepared its Comprehensive
  Financial  Report for June  30,  Annual Financial Report( CAFR),  which has been audited by our outside
  2019  independent audit firm Rogers, Anderson,  Malody & Scott, LLP ( RAMS).
  The CAFR reflects the financial position and operating activities of the City for
  the fiscal year ending June 30, 2019. A full copy of the report can be
  accessed on the City' s website.

  Brad Welebir, from Rogers, Anderson,  Malody & Scott, LLP ( RAMS) Audit
  Firm stated that as part of the Financial Statement audit, RAMS has issued
  their Report on Internal Control over Financial Reporting and on Compliance
  and Other Matters. This report is required for audits performed in Accordance
  with Government Auditing Standards.  Brad from RAMS also presented their
  concluding Auditor Letter to the City Council pertaining to the audited financial
  statements for the year ended June 30, 2019. This communication is required
  under Statement on Auditing Standards No. 114. Additionally, Brad from

  RAMS also prepared the Addendum to the Annual Progress Report of the
  Housing Successor of the City of La Verne required under Senate Bill 314
  pertaining to the City' s housing activities which are also included for Council' s
  consideration.

  Brad Welebir from Rogers, Anderson, Malody& Scott, LLP ( RAMS) Audit
  Firm, reported that no finding of concern were found. He stated that the
  Finance Staff was very  cooperative  throughout  the audit.  He stated that the

  Finance Department was doing a really good job and the City is in compliance.

  Mayor Kendrick called for public comment on this matter.

  La Verne resident asked where the pension funding stood in the report.

  It was moved by Carder, seconded by Hepburn, and unanimously carried to
  receive and file the Comprehensive Annual Financial Report, Report on
  Internal Control over Financial Reporting and on Compliance and Other
  Matters, and Auditor Letter to the City Council for the year ended June 30,
  2019.

 9.  Public Comment  This was the time set aside for anyone wishing to address the City Council on
  items not listed in any other place  on  the agenda. Mayor Kendrick  called for

  public comment.
   City Council Minutes, Monday, February 3, 2020, Page 7

  Barbara Rugeley, League of Women Voters, Mt Baldy Area, introduced the
  new League of Women Voters La Verne Observer Carrie Coolbaugh who will
  be attending City Council meetings.

  Krista Chakmak, longtime La Verne resident stated she is supporting Measure
  LV and gave her reasons.

  Jim Murphy, La Verne resident spoke about a brochure mailed out to residents
  opposing Tim Hepburn for Mayor and what was on the brochure. He spoke in
  length about why he is opposing him.

  David McElwain, La Verne resident spoke in favor of Measure LV.

  Richard Perasso, La Verne resident asked if the La Verne Fire Department
  employees have been asked how they feel about problems with the City.

  George Henderson, Old Town La Verne Business Improvement District
  commended the La Verne Police Department for doing a great job in keeping
  the City safe. He spoke in support of Measure LV.

  Mark Gutierrez, President of the La Verne Police Officers' Association spoke in
  support of Measure LV and urged residents to vote Yes to secure La Verne.

  Rick Bowen, La Verne resident thanked the Public Works Department Staff
  and Assistant City Manager/ Public Works Director Keesey for the great job at
  Golden Hills Road and Esperanza during the Christmas  season.  He
  commented that not everyone has an internal source from City as others do.

  Lynn Del Toro, La Verne resident spoke about Marshall Canyon Golf Course
  and the efforts of Council Member Hepburn and others working with the
  County of Los Angeles in saving the golf course.

  Anna Anderson, La Verne resident spoke about Fire Station 3 brownout and
  the issues with the Fire Department and it always coming up.  She urged
  everyone to work it out and to move forward.

  Chris Gendreau, Old Town Business Improvement District, stated that the
  La Verne Fire Department wants to go County and stated that Mayor Kendrick
  and Council Member Hepburn should state if they are in favor or not.

  Brian Markey, La Verne resident stated he was totally against the Fire
  Department going County and the Fire employees are free to quit and join the
  Los Angeles Fire Department.

10.  Council Comments and  Council Member Hepburn stated that the vote by mail ballots were out and
  Meeting/ Conference  Reports  urged the residents to vote and to vote yes for Measure LV.

  Council Member Carder thanked Lynn del Toro for her comments on Marshall
  Canyon Golf Course. She spoke about the hard work and leadership by the
  City Manager on the Gold Line Construction and on the matter of White
  Avenue  widening.  In addition she spoke about the work on the formation of
  the EIFD and securing funding by Mayor Kendrick and City Manager Russi.
  I

  Mayor Kendrick spoke about the EIFD which will raise millions for City
  infrastructure improvements  at no cost  to the residents.  He also commended
  the City Manager for his work  in forming the EIFD.  He also spoke about when

  the City of La Verne was named " Best City to Raise a Family" in the Family
  Circle Magazine.  In addition he stated he was very concerned about things
  being said about him that were not true and he stated the true facts.
